analyst_view.overall: Early view: Benfica top the table with four wins from four and had won seven in a row in all competitions under new coach Marco Silva when they beat Lech, with 13 league-phase goals. Plzen are 30th with 3 points and lost both home games so far (0-3 to Union, 1-2 to Levski); Benfica also sit second in Portugal, five points behind Porto, so league games around this may tempt some rotation.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean higher: Benfica's European games have averaged four goals, and Georgiy Sudakov, Gianluca Prestianni and Rafa Silva all scored against Lech. Plzen have conceded in both home games and need to attack, so a Benfica win by two or more with a Plzen goal is plausible.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Benfica out-cornered Lech comfortably and Plzen may sit deep for long spells, but a home side needing points will also push, so I stay close to the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, which is on the high side. Benfica's games have been fairly clean, but a home side under pressure chasing a dominant visitor can foul a lot, so I stay near the number until the referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots. Benfica dominate most games and Plzen should be more adventurous at home than away, so the total looks about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. I lean a little higher: Benfica's front line is in form and Plzen will have to come out to get anything, which leaves space for the kind of clear chances Benfica created against Lech.
